info.title: FortiSOAR API
info.summary: Hand-shaped subset of the FortiSOAR REST API.
info.description:
A hand-shaped OpenAPI 3.1 reference for the FortiSOAR REST API.

> **Official docs:** [FortiSOAR API Guide on docs.fortinet.com](https://docs.fortinet.com/document/fortisoar/latest/api-guide/846127). This reference is **not** official Fortinet documentation - it's a community project. Consult the official guide for the authoritative surface; use this site for endpoints that the guide doesn't cover or where live-verified shapes are useful.

> **Disclaimer.** This reference is a community effort and is **not exhaustive**. Coverage is the surface I use day-to-day; many operations are still missing. Request/response examples marked live-captured came from a real FortiSOAR; the rest are documented from the API guide and DB introspection only and are best-effort. Always validate against your own appliance before relying on it.

Pills under each operation's title show which credentials it accepts - see [Authentication](#description/authentication).

## Concepts

Responses follow the **JSON-LD + Hydra** convention. In practice that means every record has an `@id` URL you can copy and reuse as a reference, plus an `@type` (the module name) and `@context` (model URL). List endpoints wrap their results in a `hydra:member` envelope - see [Pagination & response shape](#description/pagination-response-shape).

- **IRI** - a relative URL like `/api/3/alerts/<uuid>`. Treat it as a foreign-key pointer: wherever JSON references another record, that's what you'll see. The server generates `@id` on insert; clients should not send it.
- **UUID** - 36-character hex w/ hyphens. Optional on POST: send your own to retain it for cross-system reference, or omit and read it back from the response IRI.
- **CamelCase** - every key is camelCase (`sourceId`, `dueDate`, `hydra:variableRepresentation`). Use the same convention for any custom modules.
- **Picklist values are IRIs from 7.5.0+.** Posting `"severity": "High"` is rejected; you must post `"severity": "/api/3/picklists/<value-uuid>"`. Fetch the value's IRI from `GET /api/3/picklists?listName.name=AlertSeverity&itemValue=High`. Bulk-feed paths are an exception (no validation).
- **Trigger-bypass semantics.** `POST /api/ingest-feeds/*` and `POST /api/insert-feeds/*` skip on-create playbook triggers (intentional, for high-volume feeds). `POST /api/3/insert/*` (with optional `__bulk: true` for batching) does **not** skip triggers.

## Authentication

Three documented methods; only two are recommended.

| Method | Header | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| **API key** (recommended) | `Authorization: API-KEY <key>` (note literal space) | Appliances, scheduled jobs, long-lived integrations. Mint via Settings -> Security Management -> Access Keys. |
| **Bearer JWT** | `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` | Short-lived / interactive use. Obtain from `POST /auth/authenticate`. Default TTL ~30 min; re-auth on 401. |
| HMAC | (legacy) | Documented in the public PDF for completeness. Out of scope here - most clients should use API key. |

Some endpoints accept only one method. Each operation carries pills next to its title, measured against live FortiSOAR:

- **API key** / **JWT** in green - that credential works. In red and struck through - it does not.
- **Not tested** - the call is too destructive to run against a live box, so it is unverified.
- **Not found** - the route answers 404 to every credential, so it does not exist on the versions measured.
- A blue version pill (**8.0.1+**) - the FortiSOAR version that introduced the operation.

Calls that need no credential (`POST /auth/authenticate`, `/api/version`, `/api/public/license`) have no pills.

The operation's lock icon / auth selector lists only the methods in green.


## Pagination & response shape

Every `GET /api/3/<plural>` returns a Hydra paged collection:

```json
{
  "@context": "/api/3/contexts/Alert",
  "@id": "/api/3/alerts",
  "@type": "hydra:PagedCollection",
  "hydra:totalItems": 1247,
  "hydra:itemsPerPage": 30,
  "hydra:firstPage": "/api/3/alerts",
  "hydra:nextPage":  "/api/3/alerts?$page=2",
  "hydra:lastPage":  "/api/3/alerts?$page=42",
  "hydra:member": [ ... ],
  "hydra:search":  { "@type": "hydra:IriTemplate", "hydra:template": "/api/3/alerts{?}", "hydra:mapping": [] }
}
```

`hydra:member` is the array. The rest is navigation/metadata.

### Reserved query parameters

| Param | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `$limit` | 30 | Max **5000** (server-enforced cap). |
| `$page` | 1 | 1-indexed. |
| `$orderby` | - | `field` or `-field` for desc. Body `sort[]` is the equivalent on `/api/query`. |
| `$relationships` | `false` | Controls whether linked modules appear in the response. When `true`, related collections (e.g. an alert's `tasks`, `indicators`, `assets`) are populated. When `false`, those collections are **left out entirely** - not returned as empty arrays. Single-value links (`severity`, `status`, `createUser`, etc.) are always returned as full record objects regardless of this flag. |
| `$export` | `false` | Strips identity fields so the result re-imports cleanly. Used by export UI. |
| `$partial` | `false` | When `true`, `hydra:totalItems` is omitted (skips `COUNT(*)`). Useful when paging blindly. |
| `$search` | - | See [Query reference](#description/query-reference) - top-level token, distinct from the per-field `search` operator. |
| `$fields` | - | **Power user** - `?$fields=uuid,name,steps` returns only those columns. Big response-size win on bulk pulls. |

### Power-user URL filtering

These work on every `/api/3/<plural>` endpoint and cover ~90% of what `/api/query/*` does without a body:

- **Nested dot notation** traverses relationships at any depth: `?triggerStep.stepType.name=cybersponse.post_create&triggerStep.arguments.resources$exists=alerts&isActive=true`. Either `.` or `__` works (`steps__stepType__name` ≡ `steps.stepType.name`).
- **Operators** are appended with `$`: `?eventCount$gte=10&eventCount$lt=20`, `?status__itemValue$in=Open|Resolved|InProgress`. Default operator (no `$op` suffix) is `eq`.
- **Existence on collections**: `<rel>.<arrayField>$exists=value` - "find playbooks whose trigger covers this module". Example: `triggerStep.arguments.resources$exists=alerts`.
- **Multiple parts are ANDed.** No way to OR via URL params - repeating a key (`?field=A&field=B`) returns `400 Bad Request`. Use the body endpoint for OR.

## Query reference

Three distinct query surfaces - pick by use case:

| Surface | Endpoint | Filter | Aggregations | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| URL-param | `GET /api/3/<resource>?...` | single AND chain | none | Simple lookups; everything ANDs together |
| Body | `POST /api/query/<resource>` | nested AND/OR groups | yes | Anything non-trivial; complex filters; counts |
| Global | `POST /api/search` | keyword `q` | none | Cross-module text search (Elasticsearch) |

### Request body shape

```jsonc
{
  "logic": "AND" | "OR",
  "filters": [
    { "field": "<path>", "operator": "<op>", "value": <val>, "type": "<type>"? },   // leaf
    { "logic": "AND" | "OR", "filters": [ ... ] }                                    // nested group
  ],
  "sort":       [ { "field": "<path>", "direction": "asc" | "desc" } ],
  "aggregates": [ { "operator": "<op>", "field": "<path>", "alias": "<name>" } ]
}
```

Pagination + `$search` ride on the **query string** (`?$limit=30&$page=2&$search=fortinet`); body fields named `page`/`pageSize`/`limit` are silently ignored.

### Field operators

| Operator | Behavior | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `eq` | exact equality | Default if `operator` omitted. For association IRIs, the UUID is extracted before comparison. |
| `neq` | exact inequality | |
| `lt`, `lte`, `gt`, `gte` | numeric / date comparisons | With `type: "datetime"` + a numeric value, the value is treated as epoch. |
| `in` | match any of N | Accepts `[...]` array or a `\|`-delimited string. **Lowercases** string values. Association IRIs -> UUIDs. |
| `nin` | NOT IN | Generated SQL is `NOT IN (...) OR field IS NULL` - **includes NULL rows by design**. |
| `like` | SQL LIKE | **Lowercases** the value; matches against `LOWER(field)` for non-JSON columns. Wildcards `%` `_`. |
| `notlike` | SQL NOT LIKE | Excluded from `ALL_OPERATORS` whitelist - works in practice but may be UI-hidden / pending deprecation. |
| `contains` | JSON containment | For `jsonb` columns. |
| `exists` | JSON path existence | Undocumented in the public guide; works against JSON-typed columns. |
| `isnull` | `true` -> IS NULL, `false` -> IS NOT NULL | |
| `search` | per-field full-text | **Source-only.** Declared in the parser but every wire form returns 500. Use `$search` instead. |

### Aggregations

| Operator | DQL | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `fields`, `select` | `SELECT field AS alias` | Selecting raw fields; **does not flip query into aggregate mode**. |
| `count` | `COUNT(field)` | `field: "*"` -> root alias. |
| `countdistinct` | `COUNT(DISTINCT field)` | Omitted from `ALL_OPERATORS` whitelist but works at builder layer. |
| `groupby` | adds `GROUP BY field` | Pair with a metric (`count`/`sum`/...). |
| `distinct` | `DISTINCT field` | |
| `sum`, `max`, `min` | corresponding SQL | |
| `avg`, `median` | corresponding SQL | Constants exist; **omitted from whitelist** (still emit). |

A query is treated as aggregate iff `aggregates[]` contains anything other than `fields`/`select`. That changes the response shape - `hydra:member` becomes aggregate rows instead of records.

### Field projection with selectFields and ignoreFields

Body-level allow/deny lists for the response shape. Lighter than aggregations - they don't flip the query into aggregate mode, they just shape what each `hydra:member` record contains.

```jsonc
{
  "logic": "AND",
  "filters": [ { "field": "status.itemValue", "operator": "eq", "value": "Open" } ],
  "__selectFields": ["id", "uuid", "name", "severity", "status", "createDate"]
}
```

```jsonc
{
  "logic": "AND",
  "filters": [ { "field": "createDate", "operator": "gte", "value": 1735689600, "type": "datetime" } ],
  "__ignoreFields": ["createDate", "createUser", "modifyDate", "modifyUser", "@settings"]
}
```

Use one or the other, not both. Common for **bulk export** (drop audit/ownership fields) and **bulk dashboards** (only fetch what the tile renders). Equivalent to the URL-side `$fields` projection on `GET /api/3/<resource>` but available on the body grammar where you also have OR / nested filters / aggregates.

### Top-level search URL parameter

Available on **both** `GET /api/3/<resource>` and `POST /api/query/<resource>`:

```
GET  /api/3/workflows?$search=fortinet
POST /api/query/workflows?$search=fortinet  + body filters
```

- Case-insensitive substring across the entity's "searchable fields" (per-entity set).
- Tokenized when multi-word.
- AND-combinable with body filters / URL filters.
- No min-length gate (`$search=a` happily matches).
- **Top-level only.** Putting `{"$search": "x"}` inside the body's `filters[]` is silently ignored.

### Elasticsearch global search endpoint

Different beast. Use for "global search bar" UX; for deterministic per-entity filtering use `/api/query` instead.

```jsonc
{
  "q": "fortinet phishing",         // **min 3 chars** enforced
  "index": ["alerts", "incidents"], // required, non-empty
  "size": 30, "offset": 0,
  "searchType": "_default",
  "modifyDateGte": 0, "modifyDateLte": 0
}
```

- Multi-index in one call.
- Team / RBAC scoped automatically (joins `accessibleTeamIris`).
- 3-character minimum enforced server-side.
- `400 TypeError` from this route means the downstream `cyops-search` MQ consumer is unhealthy, not that the body shape is wrong. Check `systemctl status cyops-search` on the appliance.

### Persisted queries

Persisted queries are stored in `/api/3/queries` (ad-hoc), `/api/3/system_queries` (system-owned), and `/api/3/user_queries` (user-saved). They're *inputs* you copy into the body of `POST /api/query/<resourceShortName>` - there is no separate execute route that takes a query ID. To run a saved query, GET the query record and POST its body to `/api/query/<shortName>`. (`POST /api/query/<shortName>/<id>/<field>` is a related but distinct endpoint - relationship-walk on a record, not query execute.)

## Audit gateway quirks

`POST /api/gateway/audit/activities` is the workhorse for SIEM-style log pulls. It has nine traps worth knowing about up-front.

1. **Slice pagination, no totals.** The response has no `totalElements` / `totalPages` / `last` (intentional - the repository skips `COUNT(*)` for performance). Detect end-of-data via empty `content` or `content.length < limit`. For totals, call the sibling `/count` endpoint.
2. **Default `limit` is 10 if you misname the param.** Conventions like `size`, `pageSize`, `max` are silently dropped and the server applies its default of 10. Only `limit` works.
3. **`filterParams: { ... }` wrapper is silently ignored.** Filters must be at the top level of the body; anything nested under `filterParams` is dropped.
4. **Arrays don't work for any filter.** `{"operation": ["Login Success"]}` (single-element array) silently no-ops. `{"operation": ["A", "B"]}` returns 400. To get multiple ops server-side, make multiple calls and merge.
5. **`user` is not filterable, only `userId`.** `{"user": "Jane Doe"}` is silently ignored. `{"userId": "jdoe"}` works.
6. **`search` is brittle.** `{"search": "Login"}` returned 0 hits even with many "Login" titles in the data. Probably searches a specific subset of fields with prefix-only matching. Don't rely on it.
7. **No server-side sort control.** Records arrive `id DESC` (newest first). No `sort` param honored. Sort client-side if you need anything else.
8. **`displayName` arrives dirty.** Some records have extra whitespace, embedded UUIDs, even unrelated text from other fields. Sanitize on read.
9. **JWT lifetime is short.** Default ~30 min; long-running syncs need to re-auth on 401, or use an API key where the operation takes one.

The 45-value `operation` enum is in the `AuditOperation` schema; fetch it dynamically from `GET /api/gateway/audit/operations`.

## Workflows & triggers

Run control lives under `/api/wf/*`. The endpoints below cover the most common control flows; less-used ones (`historical-workflows/*`, `expressions/*`, `dynamic-variable/*`) are tracked as a future expansion.

- `POST /api/wf/api/workflows/{pk}/start/` - manually queue.
- `POST /api/wf/api/workflows/{pk}/resume/` - resume a `paused` run. **Not for `awaiting`** manual-input runs - those use `wfinput_resume` (below).
- `GET /api/wf/api/workflows/{pk}/retry/` - retry a failed run from the failed step. **GET, not the guide's POST** (POST answers 405 on 8.0.0).
- `POST /api/wf/api/workflows/{pk}/approval/` - approval-step shortcut.

**Resuming an `awaiting` manual-input run** (verified live end-to-end; the run advances to `finished`):

1. `GET /api/wf/api/workflows/{run_pk}/?step_detail=true` → the run's awaiting execution-step ids (the correlation anchor).
2. `POST /api/wf/api/manual-wf-input/list_wfinput/` → the pending input whose `step_id` is one of those ids → `manual_input_id`. (`workflow` on the list member is an *encrypted* token, not the run pk, so `step_id` is the only honest link.)
3. `POST /api/wf/api/manual-wf-input/{manual_input_id}/retrieve_wfinput/` → `response_mapping.options[]` (the buttons; each has a `step_iri`).
4. `POST /api/wf/api/workflows/{run_pk}/wfinput_resume/` with `{input, step_iri: <chosen option's step_iri>, step_id, manual_input_id}` (add `approved: <bool>` for `is_approval` gates).

**Correction (was wrong here before):** `wfinput_resume` is the **real** path - it is NOT a decoy. `PUT /api/wf/api/manual-wf-input/{id}/` returns 200 but does **not** advance the run; don't use it to resume.

**Simpler linkage (live-verified on 8.0.0-6034):** the plain `GET /api/wf/api/manual-wf-input/` collection rows carry `workflow` as the **numeric run pk** (e.g. `144042`) - the same pk `wfinput_resume` wants - so a script that triggered the run itself can match its pending input by run pk alone, no `step_detail` correlation needed. `user` on the resume body is a `/api/3/people` IRI (resolve an admin from `GET /api/3/people`); omitting it 500s.

### Triggers

Three ways to fire a playbook from outside:

- **`POST /api/triggers/1/{name}`** - hits a Custom API Endpoint trigger (named via the trigger config). Allows alternate auth (Basic / no-auth) for external webhooks, by design - keeps the core API token-locked while letting webhook senders use simpler auth.
- ~~`POST /api/triggers/1/deferred/{name}`~~ - documented as the async variant (202) but **not routed on 8.0.0**: every name 404s before authentication. Use the sync route above.
- **`POST /api/triggers/1/notrigger/{workflowId}`** - direct execution of a workflow by UUID, bypassing trigger conditions. Useful for testing.
- **`POST /api/triggers/1/action/{routeUuid}`** - record-context execution via an action trigger's `route` uuid (from the playbook definition's trigger step). Answers `{"task_ids": [...]}` (plural), unlike `notrigger`'s scalar `task_id`.

The notifier service has additional fan-out via STOMP-over-WebSocket at `/websocket/` (server pushes workflow updates on `/topic/workflows/`). No REST surface; out of scope here.

### Triggering a playbook with an API key and tracking the task

Worked end-to-end flow against a Custom API Endpoint trigger: fire the playbook, capture the `task_id`, poll the workflow log until it reaches a terminal state, then fetch full execution details. The `deferred/` variant is not routed on 8.0.0; `notrigger/<workflowId>` and `action/<routeUuid>` fire with the same pattern (only the trigger URL changes).

**1. Fire the trigger.** `POST /api/triggers/1/<endpoint-name>` with the body the playbook expects. Auth header is `Authorization: API-KEY <key>` (literal space, not a colon). The response always contains a `task_id` - that is the handle you track, not the workflow IRI.

```python
import requests

BASE_URL = "https://fortisoar.example.com"
HEADERS = {
    "Authorization": f"API-KEY {API_KEY}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
}

resp = requests.post(
    f"{BASE_URL}/api/triggers/1/lookup_ip",
    headers=HEADERS,
    json={"value": "1.1.1.2"},
    verify=False,
)
resp.raise_for_status()
task_id = resp.json().get("task_id") or resp.json()["data"]["task_id"]
```

The `task_id` field sometimes sits at the top level and sometimes inside `data` depending on the trigger flavor - check both. Synchronous triggers return 200; `deferred/` returns 202 with the same envelope.

**2. Poll the workflow log by `task_id`.** The workflows endpoint indexes runs by `task_id` and returns the parent run when filtered with `parent_wf__isnull=True` (skips child sub-workflows). Order by `-modified` and take the first hit.

```python
url = (
    f"{BASE_URL}/api/wf/api/workflows/"
    f"?format=json&limit=1&offset=0&ordering=-modified"
    f"&task_id={task_id}&parent_wf__isnull=True"
)
log = requests.get(url, headers=HEADERS, verify=False).json()["hydra:member"][0]
status = log["status"]   # pending | running | finished | failed | terminated | skipped
workflow_id = log["@id"].rstrip("/").split("/")[-1]
```

Terminal states are **`finished`**, **`failed`**, **`terminated`**, **`skipped`**. Anything else (`pending`, `running`, `awaiting`, ...) means keep polling. An empty `hydra:member` array right after trigger is normal - the log row is written on first executor pickup, not on trigger receipt.

**3. Fetch full execution details.** Once terminal, hit the workflow record directly:

```python
details = requests.get(
    f"{BASE_URL}/api/wf/api/workflows/{workflow_id}/?format=json",
    headers=HEADERS, verify=False,
).json()
```

- **`details["result"]`** - the playbook's final output (the output of the last executed step). This is what 90% of callers want.
- **`details["name"]`** - playbook name.
- **`details["status"]`** - same terminal status as the log row.
- **Per-step outputs** - the workflow record also carries a step-execution array (field name varies by FortiSOAR version); each entry has a step name + its output. Useful when you need an intermediate step's value rather than the last one. Inspect `details.keys()` on your appliance to confirm the field name before relying on it.

If the last step produced no output, `result` is `null` even on `status: finished` - that's expected, not an error.

**Gotchas observed in practice:**

- **Poll interval.** 5 s is a sensible floor; the executor batches log writes. Tighter polling just multiplies the request count without buying any latency.
- **No `task_id` in response.** Usually means the trigger name is wrong (404 was masked by a redirect) or the playbook is inactive. The endpoint returns 200 with an empty body in some edge cases - always check before subscripting.
- **`parent_wf__isnull=True` is required** for playbooks that fan out via `Execute Sub Playbook`. Without it the first match may be a child run that finishes before the parent.
 - **API-KEY vs Bearer.** An API key lasts for its validity period (1 to 365 days, set when it is created), so it suits long-running tracker scripts; a JWT typically dies after ~30 minutes mid-poll.

## Modules

A **module** is FortiSOAR's unit of schema: a named table with a list of fields
("attributes"). Every record collection (`alerts`, `incidents`, custom modules) is
backed by a module definition. The schema lives in two stores, and a third endpoint
moves changes between them:

- **Staging** (`/api/3/staging_model_metadatas`) - the editable draft. Creating a module
  or changing a field edits staging only; nothing is live yet.
- **Published** (`/api/3/model_metadatas`) - the committed schema records are read from.
  `GET /api/3/model_metadatas` is the drift-resistant source of truth for what fields a
  module actually has on this appliance.
- **Publish** is a single appliance-wide `PUT /api/publish` that promotes *all* pending
  staged changes to live. It is **not per-module** - one illegally-named draft anywhere
  can fail the whole migrate, so validate drafts before publishing.

### Field types - two axes

Every field (attribute) carries a **storage type** (`type`) and a **display type**
(`formType`). These are different axes and a correct field needs both:

- `type` is the column kind the platform stores: `string`, `integer`, `float`,
  `boolean`, `picklists`, `object`, `array`, or a target module type for a relationship.
  There is **no `text` storage type** - text-like fields store `string`. Publishing a
  field whose `type` is `text` fails validation ("Attribute type 'text' does not
  exist").
- `formType` is the editor widget: `text`, `textarea`, `richtext`, `html`, `email`,
  `url`, `phone`, `password`, `filehash`, `ipv4`, `ipv6`, `domain`, `file`, `integer`,
  `decimal`, `datetime`, `checkbox`, `json`, `object`, `picklist`,
  `multiselectpicklist`, `lookup`, `manyToMany`, `oneToMany`.

A `lookup` is a one-directional many-to-one pointer (no reverse field is created). A
`manyToMany` is a collection relationship; with the **default** inverse the platform
auto-creates the reverse field, with a **custom** `inversedField` you create the mirror
yourself. A `oneToMany` needs a matching `lookup` on its target - it will not publish
without one.

### Publish blast radius

Publish is synchronous in effect but asynchronous in execution - the PUT only *starts*
the migrate; the backup + commit then runs server-side, during which some surfaces may
be briefly unavailable. The impact is version- and change-dependent:

- On older builds every publish - even a no-op - runs the full backup + migrate + cache
  rebuild, during which the entire `/api/3` surface returns 503 for the whole window
  (~50-57s observed).
- On newer builds the impact is greatly reduced. A minor field-only edit (toggling
  *visibility* or setting *required-by-condition*) commits in ~3s with no observable
  outage. A **structural** change (adding a field/module) takes longer (~30s) and
  disrupts only the *record/query layer*: record-list endpoints return transient 404
  for ~13s and `/api/query` returns 400/401 for ~2.5s while the migrate runs - **not** a
  global 503. Module-metadata, view-resolve, and picklist surfaces stay available
  throughout. That record-layer blip is instance-wide, not scoped to the changed module.

`GET /api/publish/error` reports the last publish's status
(`{"status": "Success"|"Failed"|..., "last_publish_time": <epoch>}`) - it returns HTTP
400 (rather than 200) when a prior error is on record, with the same JSON body, so poll
it status-agnostically until `last_publish_time` advances.

## Imports & exports

There are **two import paths** with different semantics; the wrong choice silently fails.

| Endpoint | Body | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/3/workflow_collections` | unwrapped collection (`{name, description, visible, uuid, workflows: [...]}`) | strict create. **409 `UniqueConstraintViolationException`** on UUID collision. |
| `POST /api/3/import_jobs` | export-style envelope (`{type, data, macros, exported_tags}`) | **does not import the JSON inline** - see gotcha below. |

### The import_jobs gotcha

The import-job record has fields `file`, `status`, `options`, `type` - and **no `data` field**. The server's request decoder silently drops unknown keys and accepts your payload's outer `type` (e.g. `"workflow_collections"`), overriding the expected `"Import Wizard"` value. Result: 200 OK, no actual import.

**Real flow:**

1. `POST /api/3/files/` (multipart) - upload the JSON blob.
2. `POST /api/3/import_jobs` with `{file: "/api/3/files/<uuid>", type: "Import Wizard", options: {...}}`.
3. The import worker picks up the job and applies the file.

### Default mergeType is merge_append

A naive re-POST to `import_jobs` returns 200 but **silently skips** any playbook whose UUID *or* `(name, collection)` matches an existing record. For dev-loop overwrite semantics, attach explicit options:

```json
{
  "type": "Import Wizard",
  "file": "/api/3/files/<uuid>",
  "options": {
    "playbooks": {
      "include": true,
      "values": [
        {"uuid": "<col-uuid>", "name": "<col-name>",
         "include": true, "mergeType": "merge_replace",
         "includeSchedules": true}
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

| `mergeType` | Collection-level | Workflow-level |
|---|---|---|
| `rename` | suffix ` (1)`, ` (2)`... until unique; new UUID | re-rolls UUIDs |
| `replace` | DELETE + insert | (whole collection replaced) |
| `merge_replace` | keep collection, replace workflows | UUID-or-name match -> DELETE -> insert new |
| `merge_append` (default) | keep collection, add new | UUID-or-name match -> skip incoming |

### Entity uniqueness constraints

| Entity | Constraint | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `WorkflowCollection.name` | `nullable=false`, **`unique=true`** instance-wide | rename or DELETE the existing one before re-import. |
| `Workflow` | `UniqueConstraint(columns={"name", "collection"})` | unique **per collection**, not globally. |
| `Workflow.aliasName` | `nullable=true`, no unique constraint | safe to emit `null`. |
| `WorkflowStep.name` | `nullable=false`, length 255 | required. |
| `WorkflowRoute.sourceStep` / `targetStep` | FK `nullable=false`, `onDelete="CASCADE"` | both required; deleting a step cascades its routes. |

### Cross-collection UUID collision

If a workflow UUID matches one already in a *different* collection, FortiSOAR re-rolls a fresh UUID for the workflow **and all its steps**. Deterministic UUIDs are stable **within a collection** only, not portable across.

tags.name: System

tags.name: Notifications
tags.description: Per-user system (bell-icon) notifications under `/api/rule/api/system-notification/`. Note the non-standard `/api/rule/` namespace and that the list endpoint is POST, not GET.

tags.name: Records (generic)
tags.description: Every module that stores records is available at `/api/3/<plural>` with the same list + create / get / update / delete shape (list responses are wrapped in a `hydra:member` envelope - see [Pagination & response shape](#description/pagination-response-shape)). The operations below - list / create on `/api/3/{collection}` and get / update / delete on `/api/3/{collection}/{uuid}` - document that shared shape. The **Alerts** endpoints are a worked example.

tags.name: Alerts
tags.description: Concrete CRUD on the `alerts` collection - representative of every record module (`incidents`, `indicators`, `tasks`, `assets`, `people`, ...).

tags.name: Bulk operations
tags.description: High-throughput insert/update/delete/upsert and feed-ingest paths. Note: `/api/ingest-feeds/*` and `/api/insert-feeds/*` skip on-create playbook triggers; `POST /api/3/insert/*` does not.

tags.name: Query
tags.description: Three search surfaces: URL-param (AND only), POST `/api/query/*` body grammar (full AND/OR + aggregates), and global Elasticsearch (`/api/search`). See operation descriptions for when to use which.

tags.name: Audit
tags.description: Audit log search + retention. Returns one page at a time with no total count - call `/count` separately if you need it. Filters are top-level only and accept exactly one value.

tags.name: Playbook runs
tags.description: Track and control playbook runs after they start: status by `task_id`, run detail, step history, resume / retry / approve. Lives under `/api/wf/*`.

tags.name: Run a playbook
tags.description:
Start a playbook from the API. Pick the route by how the playbook is triggered:

| Playbook's trigger | Route | pyfsr |
|---|---|---|
| Any (by playbook UUID; trigger conditions skipped) | `POST /api/triggers/1/notrigger/{workflowId}` | `client.playbooks.trigger(name_or_uuid)` |
| Custom API Endpoint | `POST /api/triggers/1/{name}` | `client.playbooks.trigger_by_name(name)` |
| Custom API Endpoint, run on a worker (202) - **not found on 8.0.0** | `POST /api/triggers/1/deferred/{name}` | `client.playbooks.trigger_by_name(name, deferred=True)` |
| Manual (record action button) | `POST /api/triggers/1/action/{routeUuid}` | `client.playbooks.trigger_action(route_uuid, module=..., record_uuid=...)` |

Every route answers with a `task_id`. Track it with `GET /api/wf/api/workflows/?task_id=<task_id>&parent_wf__isnull=True` (see **Playbook runs**), or call `client.playbooks.run_and_wait(...)`. Worked example: [Triggering a playbook with an API key and tracking the task](#description/triggering-a-playbook-with-an-api-key-and-tracking-the-task).

tags.name: Scheduled tasks
tags.description: Workflow-engine periodic jobs under `/api/wf/api/scheduled/` - the platform-shipped schedules (Reclaim Disk Space, Purge Executed Playbook Logs, Archive Data) plus user-created cron schedules that run a playbook. Each row is a periodic task with a nested `crontab` and a `kwargs.wf_iri` pointing at the workflow. The row `id` is a per-request Fernet token - resolve by `name` for any non-immediate use.

tags.name: Connectors
tags.description:
Full connector lifecycle. Per-action request shape comes from each connector's `info.json`.

**Flow - install → configure → execute → uninstall:**

1. **Install from `.tgz`** - `POST /api/3/solutionpacks/install?$type=connector&$replace=true` (multipart, field `file` = the binary). Response carries the integer connector `id`.
2. **Create a config** - `POST /api/integration/configuration/` with `name`, `connector` (integer id from step 1), and `config` (the connector's field values). Add `agent` only if you want the connector to run on a **remote agent**; omit it to use the appliance's self-agent. Response carries `config_id` (uuid).
3. **Execute an action** - `POST /api/integration/execute/` with `connector` name, `version`, `operation`, `config` (the uuid from step 2), and `params`.
4. **Health-check** - `GET /api/integration/connectors/healthcheck/{name}/{version}/?config=<uuid>` for the cheap variant (uses an existing config), or the POST form when re-sending a full config inline.
5. **Cleanup** - `DELETE /api/integration/configuration/{config_id}/` (uuid + trailing slash), then `DELETE /api/integration/connectors/{id}/` (integer id + trailing slash). The trailing slash is mandatory - without it you'll see `403 Could not validate HMAC fingerprint`.

**Targeting a remote agent:** to run a connector on a remote agent instead of the self-agent, either include `agent` in the `POST /api/integration/configuration/` body (existing config on a remote agent), or use the dedicated remote-install routes: `POST /api/integration/install-connector/` with `name`, `version`, `agent_id` to push the connector to a specific agent; `PUT` to upgrade and `DELETE` to uninstall on the same path. `GET /api/integration/connectors/agents/{name}/{version}/` lists which agents already have the connector installed, and `GET /api/integration/agent-heartbeat/{agent}/` probes the SME bus to that agent.

tags.name: Agents
tags.description:
Remote-agent records, SME router discovery, and the per-agent installer download.

**Flow - discover router → create agent → download installer → verify:**

1. **Find the router** - `GET /api/3/routers` and read the first member's `@id` (router IRI) and `certificate` (CA PEM for the agent VM). Empty collection means SME is not enabled on the master; run `sudo csadm secure-message-exchange enable` first.
2. **Create the record** - `POST /api/3/agents` with `name`, `router` (IRI from step 1), and `installerType` (bash or docker picklist IRI). Response carries `uuid`, `agentId`, `encryptionKey`, `username`, `password`, `vhost` - **the secrets are returned only once**.
3. **Download the installer** - `POST /api/integration/agent-installer/` with the `agentId` from step 2. Response is a binary installer (`application/octet-stream`).
4. **Verify** - poll `GET /api/3/agents/{uuid}` until `configurationHealth.itemValue` reaches `Remote Node Connected`. New records start in `Awaiting Remote Node Connection`.

**Self-agent constants:** the appliance's own Self agent record is hardcoded at uuid `973c17df-bb4b-41e5-b59c-a408666fdf27` on every install (the parent tenant uuid is `b3a700f7-00be-4ef9-90c6-3c8fe6e1be63`). Its `agentId` - the runtime `masterId` - varies per appliance; read it from `GET /api/3/agents/{self-uuid}`.

tags.name: Modules
tags.description: Module and field schema: discover the published data model (`model_metadatas`), edit drafts in staging (`staging_model_metadatas`), and commit changes appliance-wide with `PUT /api/publish`. Each module is a staging record with an `attributes` list; every field has a storage `type` (the column kind) and a display `formType` (the editor widget) - two distinct axes. Publish is **appliance-wide**, not per-module: one `PUT /api/publish` promotes every pending staged change across the whole instance. See the [Modules](#description/modules) introduction for the staging/publish model and field-type rules.

tags.name: Metadata
tags.description: Picklist taxonomies + values, Hydra `@context` type docs, and the auto-generated full API listing (handy for discovering endpoints not documented here).

tags.name: Files
tags.description: Attachment upload. Required as the first step of import-job ingestion.

tags.name: Widgets
tags.description: Widget upload (shared with the connector install path), publish, export, and delete. The publish step loads the development manifest and PUTs it back with publish flags - the same flow the Content-Hub UI's Publish button drives.

tags.name: Views
tags.description: View templates that control how module list and detail pages render. `GET /api/views/1/app` returns the left-hand navigation; `/api/views/1/{name}` is the per-template CRUD surface.

tags.name: Workflow tools
tags.description: Global ("dynamic") variables referenced in playbooks as `{{ globalVars.<name> }}`. List and create via `/api/wf/api/dynamic-variable/`.

tags.name: Access management
tags.description:
API keys, roles, teams.

**Flow - create → bind → use → lifecycle → revoke:** run steps 1, 2, 4 and 5 with a JWT. An API key cannot manage keys: `/api/auth/*` refuses it, and so does creating or changing an `api_keys` binding.

1. **Create the API-key user** - `POST /api/auth/users` with body `{"type": 9, "status": 1, "api_key_validity": <1..365>}`. All three are integers - the published PDF shows quoted strings, which the appliance rejects with 400. Response carries the user `uuid` and the plaintext key.
2. **Bind it to roles and teams** - `POST /api/3/api_keys` with `name`, `roles` (IRIs), `teams` (IRIs), and `userId` (the uuid from step 1). Required to make the key actually usable.
3. **Read the scope** - `GET /api/3/api_keys/{uuid}` for one binding, or `GET /api/3/api_keys` for the full list.
4. **Lifecycle operations** - `PUT /api/auth/users` with `uuid`, `key_type: API_KEY`, and `operation` ∈ `{REVOKE, ACTIVATE, DEACTIVATE, REGENERATE, RESET_VALIDITY}`. `REGENERATE` and `RESET_VALIDITY` also need `api_key_validity`.
5. **Bulk fetch with plaintext** - `POST /api/auth/query/users` with `{users: [<uuid>, ...], show_api_key: true}` (only returns plaintext for keys whose user was created with `retrievable_mode` enabled in `/api/auth/config`).

tags.name: Import / export
tags.description: Configuration import/export. Read the `import_jobs` description carefully - the inline-envelope shape is a silent no-op.

tags.name: Threat intel (TAXII)
tags.description:
TAXII 2.1 server exposing FortiSOAR threat-intel collections (FortiGuard feeds, block lists, and any custom collections you create). Discovery lives at `/api/taxii/1/`; collections, objects, and manifest endpoints follow.

The server is **read-only**: every default collection advertises `can_write: false` and `POST` to `objects/` is not routed, and there is no STIX bundle ingest route. To push threat intel into FortiSOAR, map it to module rows and use `POST /api/ingest-feeds/{module}`.

Response envelope for `objects/` and `manifest/` is `{totalItems, objects: []}` - a FortiSOAR-specific shape, not the standard TAXII 2.1 `more` / `next` cursor. Paginate with `?limit=` and `?added_after=<ISO-8601>`.

All responses use `Content-Type: application/taxii+json;version=2.1`; collection `media_types` advertise `application/stix+json;version=2.1`.

tags.name: AI
tags.description: **AI services** (8.0+). Agent configuration, LLM management, triage, enrichment, insight generation, and prompt validation.

tags.name: MCP
tags.description: **MCP tools** (8.0+). Server registration, tool catalog management, and connector-to-MCP gateway hosting.

tags.name: AI Insight
tags.description: Generate and execute multi-step investigation plans. The classic flow is `POST /api/ai/insight/plan` → `POST /api/ai/insight/plan/execute` → poll `GET /api/ai/insight/plan/{task_id}/status` → `GET /api/ai/insight/plan/{task_id}/result`. Lower-level: `POST /api/ai/insight/chain_of_thoughts` returns a single-shot reasoning trace.

tags.name: AI Agents
tags.description:
Agent execution + management. `POST /api/ai/agents/{agent_name}/trigger` and `POST /api/ai/triage/alert` kick off an agent run; `/api/ai/agents/{task_id}/{status,result,acceptance}` track it. `/api/ai/agent/*` (singular) is the agent **catalog** - import, export, activate, configure.

**The `/api/ai/triage` vs `/api/ai/agents` trap:** the AI service mounts one router under both prefixes, so the raw service OpenAPI lists both as equals, but the front-door proxy only authorises `^agents?/(.*)/trigger` (the generic trigger) and `POST /api/ai/triage/alert` specifically.  The four `/api/ai/triage/{task_id}/*` routes return 403.  Always use `/api/ai/agents/` for status, result, and acceptance - never `/api/ai/triage/` for those.

tags.name: AI Chat
tags.description: Conversational investigation. `POST /api/ai/chat/` starts or continues a thread.

tags.name: AI LLM
tags.description:
LLM provider, model, and per-tenant config catalog. Provider rows ship empty; the operator wires an OpenAI/local model with `POST /api/ai/llm/config` and verifies with `GET /api/ai/llm/config/{uuid}/verify`.  `GET /api/ai/llm/allowed-providers` lists available solution packs.

**Note:** The LLM model and provider catalogue endpoints (`GET /api/ai/llm/model`, `GET /api/ai/llm/provider`) are exposed by the AI service but return 403 through the front-door proxy - no matching permission group exists.  They are omitted from this spec.

tags.name: AI Enrichment
tags.description: Knowledge-base ingestion for the agentic RAG store. `POST /api/ai/enrich/context` retrieves enrichment, `POST /api/ai/enrich/context/index` indexes a doc, `POST /api/ai/enrich/index/build` (re)builds the vector index.

tags.name: AI Prompts
tags.description: Prompt template validation. `POST /api/ai/prompt/validate` lints a template.

tags.name: AI MCP Registry
tags.description: Register external MCP servers that the AI agents may call. `GET /api/ai/mcp` lists them, `POST /api/ai/mcp/validate` round-trips a config (handshake + auth) before persisting.

tags.name: MCP Admin
tags.description: Tool catalog CRUD on the on-appliance MCP server. `POST /mcp/add/tools` binds an installed connector's operations as MCP tools; `POST /mcp/config/{import,export}` ships tool catalogs between appliances; `GET /mcp/servers/{mcp_type}?restricted=true` returns the live registry plus the hard-coded restricted list.

tags.name: MCP Tools
tags.description: The four streamable-HTTP MCP endpoints. These speak JSON-RPC, not REST, so they are not in the upstream OpenAPI. The operations below document the wire shape and list the tools each surface exposes on a stock appliance. Hit them with `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`, run `initialize` first, capture the `mcp-session-id` response header, and reuse it on every subsequent call.

tags.name: MCP Configurations
tags.description: Full CRUD store for registered MCP servers. This is where servers are actually created (`/api/3/mcp_configurations`). The AI service only reads and validates them via `/api/ai/mcp`. Keep these tags distinct - conflating MCP Configurations with AI MCP Registry is the most common source of confusion.

tags.name: MCP Gateway
tags.description: Appliance MCP gateway for tool hosting. Manage which connectors are exposed as MCP tools, export tool catalogs, and update tool permissions.

tags.name: AI Activity
tags.description: LLM activity audit logs. Tool-call evidence from agent investigations, useful for understanding what an agent did to reach its verdict.

tags.name: AI Traces
tags.description: OpenTelemetry-style trace observability for AI agent runs. Each run produces a trace with spans (LLM calls, tool calls, sub-agent steps). Use `GET /api/ai/traces/` to list, `GET /api/ai/traces/{trace_id}` to inspect a single trace, `GET /api/ai/traces/{trace_id}/execution-tree` for the full nested run tree, and `GET /api/ai/traces/{trace_id}/spans` for a flat span list. Per-span detail: `GET /api/ai/traces/spans/{span_id}`. Token usage: `GET /api/ai/traces/tokens/{trace_id}` (per-trace) or `GET /api/ai/traces/tokens/session/{session_id}` (per-chat-session). `DELETE /api/ai/traces/delete` purges traces older than a cutoff.

post.description:
One endpoint with three behaviors keyed off the `action` discriminator:

- `action: deploy_license` - install a license on a fresh / unlicensed appliance.   Body: `license_key`, `nodeId`, `action`. Returns 200 OK on success. This is the   first-time-activation path - once a valid license is deployed, prefer the   authenticated `POST /api/auth/license` for renewals.
- `action: get_status` - poll deployment progress. Body: `action` (+ optional   `nodeId` for per-node status; omit for cluster-wide). Returns `depl_status`   (e.g. `finished`) plus either `depl_message` (cluster summary) or `depl_info`   (`source`, `user_id`, `ws_session_id`, `depl_start_time`) for a single node.
- `action: get_info` - parse a license key **without** deploying it. Body:   `license_key`, `action`. Returns `serial_no`, `expiry_time`, `hardware_key`,   `max_users`, `entitlements`, `type`, `edition`. For Subscription-type licenses,   `max_users` / `expiry_time` are only populated after deployment (they're fetched   from FDN at activation time).

action.description: Discriminator. See description for the body shape each action expects.

license_key.description: Raw license file contents. Required for `deploy_license` and `get_info`.

nodeId.description: Target node id. Required for `deploy_license`; optional for `get_status` (omit -> cluster-wide). Discoverable via `GET /api/auth/license?param=license_details` (`nodes.<id>.node.nodeId`).

parameters.name: $page

put.description:
**See:** [Concepts](#description/concepts)

Ordinary field updates: send the changed fields as a flat JSON object.

**Relationship add/remove without resending the whole record:** send `{"__link": {"<field>": ["<iri-or-module:uuid>", ...]}}` to add related records to a relationship field, or `{"__unlink": {"<field>": [...]}}` to remove them - both leave the rest of the record untouched. Each ref may be a full IRI (`/api/3/assets/<uuid>`) or `<module>:<uuid>` shorthand; a bare uuid is rejected since the related module can't be inferred. Live-verified: linking an `Asset` onto an `Alert`'s `assets` field, confirmed via `GET /api/3/alerts/<uuid>/assets`, then unlinked and reconfirmed empty. See `$relationships` above for the read side of the same relationship fields.

An API key cannot create or change `people`, `appliances` or `api_keys` records: FortiSOAR answers 403 whatever the key's role. Use a JWT for those.

get.description:
**See:** [Workflows & triggers](#description/workflows-triggers) (filter by `task_id` to track a triggered run)

Hydra-paged list of recent playbook execution logs. **Recent** here means runs that have not yet been moved to historical storage by the Playbook Log Movement task (runs every 15 minutes for completed playbooks, 60 minutes for failed/terminated; configurable in System Configuration).

For runs older than that, use `GET /api/wf/api/historical-workflows/`. To combine both stores in a single query, use `POST /api/wf/api/query/workflow_logs/?logs=all`.

Common patterns:

- `task_id=<uuid>` (with `parent_wf__isnull=True`) - look up the run created by a trigger POST,   skipping sub-playbook children.
- `ordering=-modified` + `limit=1` - newest run first.
- `template_iri=/api/3/workflows/<uuid>` - runs of a specific playbook.
- `records=/api/3/alerts/<uuid>` - runs executed against a specific record.
- `status=failed&created_after=2024-11-08&created_before=2024-11-10` - failed runs in a window.
- `tags_include=ingestion,critical&tags_exclude=system` - tag allow/deny lists.

Each `hydra:member` entry has `status` (one of `incipient`, `active`, `pending`, `running`, `finished`, `failed`, `awaiting`, `skipped`, `terminated`, `paused`) and `@id` - the trailing segment is the workflow pk used by the per-run detail GET.

parameters.name: records

post.description:
Runs a connector operation against a configured connector.

**Discovering what to send:** the `operation` key, its required `params`, and the available `config` values all come from `POST /api/integration/connectors/{id}/` (operations + configurations for the installed connector). There is no separate `/operations/` route - that POST is the operations-discovery endpoint.

**Body fields:**
- `connector` (required) - connector `name` (e.g. `hello-world`).
- `operation` (required) - operation key from the connector's `info.json`   (e.g. `reverse_text`). Discover available operations via   `POST /api/integration/connectors/{id}/` (response `operations[].operation`).
- `config` (required when the operation needs a configuration) - accepts **either**   the configuration uuid (`config_id`) **or** the configuration `name`.   Stateless operations (e.g. `cyops_utilities` formatters) still accept the field   but ignore its value. Omitting or `null` returns `INTEGRATION-12: Could not find a connector   configuration matching the given configuration id or name`.
- `version` (optional) - connector version. If omitted, the appliance resolves the   installed default version. Provide it explicitly when multiple versions are installed.
- `params` (required when the operation declares required parameters) - the action's   input payload as defined by the connector's `info.json`. Discover required params via   the same connector-detail endpoint (`operations[].parameters[]` with `required: true`).

Errors surface as 400 with an `INTEGRATION-*` or `CS-INTEGRATION-*` code in `message`.

version.description: Connector version (e.g. `1.0.4`). Optional - server resolves a default when omitted.

Connectors installed from content-hub bundles report an empty `rpm_full_name`. No 2xx body has been captured for these three operations.

get.description:
**See:** [Modules](#description/modules)

The published schema - every module with its committed fields. This is the drift-resistant source of truth for what a module actually looks like on this appliance (versus a static schema snapshot). Each entry's `@id`/`uuid` is the IRI you pass to `/api/query` `models`, and `attributes` is the field list. Add `?$relationships=true` to populate `attributes` (omitted by default).

**One module in one request:** `?type=<slug>&$relationships=true`. The `type` filter alone returns the module's header row with an **empty** `attributes` list (~1.6 KB); adding `$relationships=true` populates all fields (~227 KB for `alerts`). The result is identical to the by-uuid GET apart from an added `@context`, so there is no reason to list every module and then fetch by uuid.

parameters.name: $limit
parameters.description: Max records per page. Default 30, max 5000.

parameters.name: $page
parameters.description: 1-indexed page number.

parameters.name: $orderby
parameters.description: Sort field; prefix `-` for descending. Example: `-createDate`.

parameters.name: $relationships
parameters.description: Controls whether linked modules are included in the response. When `true`, related collections (e.g. an alert's `tasks`, `indicators`, `assets`) are populated. When `false` (default), those collections are left out of the response entirely - not returned as empty arrays. Single-value links like `severity`, `status`, `createUser` are always returned as full record objects regardless of this flag.

parameters.name: $export
parameters.description: Strip identity fields so the result re-imports cleanly.

parameters.name: $partial
parameters.description: Skip the COUNT(*) - omits hydra:totalItems for faster paging.

parameters.name: $fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated projection. **Cannot be combined with `$relationships=true` on this endpoint** - the pair returns `500 Internal Server Error` (not a 400). Use one or the other: `$fields` for a cheap module inventory, `$relationships` for full schemas.

parameters.name: $search
parameters.description: Accepted but always returns 0 matches here - ModelMetadata declares no searchable fields. Filter on `type` / `type$like` instead.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Exact-match filter on the module slug. **This is how you fetch one module's schema without knowing its uuid** - pair it with `$relationships=true` and you get the full definition in a single request instead of listing every module to find the uuid first. Case-sensitive: `alerts` matches, `Alerts` returns 0.

parameters.name: module
parameters.description: Same value as `type` on every stock module; filters identically.

parameters.name: tableName
parameters.description: Filter by the underlying table name (usually == `type`; differs after a table rename).

parameters.name: type$in
parameters.description: Multi-module fetch, pipe-delimited - one round-trip for several schemas.

parameters.name: type$like
parameters.description: Case-insensitive LIKE on the slug. Use `%` and `_` wildcards.

parameters.name: system
parameters.description: `false` returns only non-system (custom + customised) modules.

parameters.name: attributes.name
parameters.description: Dot-notation into the field list: returns every module that HAS a field with this name - the cheap answer to "which modules define `severity`?". Works with or without `$relationships=true`. Note it selects **modules**, not fields: each match still carries its complete `attributes` list, not just the matching field.

**See:** [Publish blast radius](#description/publish-blast-radius)

Promotes **every** pending staged change across the whole instance to live - not just modules you touched. The PUT only *starts* the publish; the backup + migrate then runs server-side, during which some surfaces may be briefly unavailable (see [Modules -> Publish blast radius](#description/publish-blast-radius)). Poll `GET /api/publish/error` until `last_publish_time` advances and `status` reads `Success`.

A no-op publish (nothing staged) returns right away with no migrate. One illegally-named draft anywhere can fail the whole migrate with a cryptic error that does not name the offender - validate drafts before publishing. Schema validation errors (e.g. a relationship with no matching reverse field) are returned synchronously on the PUT itself.

Live-verified on 8.0.0 with an empty staging table: `200 {"@type": "Publish", "status": "started"}`. NOT exercise-captured on the reference appliance: its staging table permanently holds ~78 foreign staged rows, and a publish here would flush those into the live schema. The live-test runner only calls this op when the staging table is empty and skips otherwise.

IRI.description: Internationalized Resource Identifier - relative URL pointing to a record. Example: /api/3/alerts/028b37fa-bb35-4e3b-8afb-a3274a8cb343.

HydraCollection.description: Standard Hydra paged collection wrapper. `hydra:member` is the array of records; the rest is navigation/pagination metadata.

QueryBody.description: Body shape for `POST /api/query/{collection}`. Logic groups, leaf filters, sort, and aggregates - see the Query reference in the introduction for full operator semantics.

logic.description: Top-level logical join. Nest by giving a child filter its own `logic` field.

oneOf.description: Nested group - recurse with its own logic + filters.

aggregates.description: Presence of any operator other than `fields`/`select` flips the response into aggregate mode (rows of aggregate values instead of records).

__selectFields.description: Allowlist of fields to return on each `hydra:member` record. Reduces response size when you only need a subset. Mutually exclusive with `__ignoreFields` (use one or the other). Lighter alternative to `aggregates: [{operator: fields, ...}]` - doesn't switch the query into aggregate mode.

name.description: Agent or pipeline that produced the run.

session_id.description: Chat session the run belongs to (aiAssistant widget runs).

end_time.description: ISO-8601; null while the run is still going.

total_tokens.description: LLM tokens consumed by the whole run.

TraceSpan.description: One span of a trace (`GET /api/ai/traces/spans/{span_id}` or a row of `.../{trace_id}/spans`). For an `LLM` span the prompt is under `input.payload.params.messages` and the reply under `output` (`content`, `tools`, `usage`, `provider`, `model`); for a `TOOL` span `output` is the tool result.

name.description: Step name (tool name for `TOOL` spans, agent name for `AGENT` spans).

input.description: Raw span input. For `TOOL` spans carries the `tool_call` (`name`, `args`).

output.description: Raw span output. For `LLM` spans: `content`, `tools`, `usage`, `provider`, `model`. For `TOOL` spans: the tool result.

TraceNode.description: A node of a trace tree (`GET /api/ai/traces/{trace_id}`, `.../execution-tree`, `.../spans/{span_id}/tree`). Carries a span summary (no full I/O -- fetch the span for that) plus its `children`.

children_truncated.description: True when the subtree was cut off (fetch the child's own tree for more).

ExecutionTree.description: A run plus every run it submitted (`GET /api/ai/traces/{trace_id}/execution-tree`) -- what the Trace Flow panel renders. An investigation typically spans ~10 traces, stitched into one `root` tree.

TaxiiDiscovery.description: TAXII server descriptor (`GET /api/taxii/1/`) -- the endpoint clients call first to confirm protocol compatibility.

max_content_length.description: Max request body size the server accepts (bytes).

TaxiiCollection.description: One TAXII collection. On FortiSOAR a collection *is* a system query: `id` maps to a system-query uuid, so a dataset is addressable as a TAXII collection.

can_read.description: Caller may read objects from this collection.

can_write.description: Caller may add objects (typically false -- publishing goes through system queries).

TaxiiManifestEntry.description: One row of a TAXII manifest: object metadata without the object body.

date_added.description: When the object entered the collection.

TaxiiObjectsEnvelope.description: STIX objects envelope (`GET /api/taxii/1/collections/{uuid}/objects[/{stixId}]`). FortiSOAR's non-standard wrapper (no TAXII 2.1 `more`/`next` semantics beyond the listed keys); paginate with `limit` + `added_after`.

ConnectorDefinition.description: A connector's definition (`POST /api/integration/connectors/{connector}/{version}/`): metadata, operations, config schema and default configuration. `client.connectors.definition()` parses this.

operations.description: The connector's operations (name, editable, sample, parameters, ...).

config_schema.description: Configuration fields the connector requires (`client.connectors.config_schema()` reads this).

message.description: What is missing or in progress (POST returns e.g. a `retrying` status).

IngestionMetadata.description: One data-ingestion configuration (`POST /api/integration/data-import/`, rows of `GET .../data-import/`): binds a connector configuration to playbooks + a data mapping.

configuration.description: Connector configuration id this ingestion binds to.

sample_data.description: Sample record captured for the mapping.

IngestionPage.description: Page envelope of `GET /api/integration/data-import/` (FortiSOAR's own paging shape, not hydra).

AgentConnectorStatus.description: Per-agent connector push result (`POST /api/integration/connectors/agents/{name}/{version}/`) -- one row per agent the connector was pushed to.

agent.description: Agent IRI the connector was pushed to.

PicklistItem.description: One option of a picklist (`GET`/`POST /api/3/picklists`). Its `@id` is the IRI records store on picklist fields; `listName` points back at the owning picklist.

listName.description: IRI (or expanded record) of the owning picklist name.

PicklistName.description: A picklist list -- the taxonomy an option belongs to (`GET`/`POST /api/3/picklist_names`). `name` is unique instance-wide (a duplicate POST 409s).

system.description: True for the shipped system picklists.

picklists.description: Embedded options (present only when the request asks for `$relationships=true`).

MCPServerConfig.description: A registered MCP server (`/api/3/mcp_configurations`). `authentication` is stored as a JSON *string* (write-only semantics: the appliance never echoes secrets).

type.description: `FSR` for built-in gateways; `Custom` for external servers.

authentication.description: Stored auth block as a JSON string (e.g. `{"type": "FSR"}`); never echoes secrets.

ModelMetadata.description: A module's metadata record (`/api/3/model_metadatas`, `/api/3/staging_model_metadatas`): table flags, display name, descriptions, and the `attributes` list that drives `src/module_to_schema.py`.

attributes.description: Field definitions (name, type, required, picklist ref, ...).

ExportJob.description: An export job (`POST /api/3/export_jobs`): polls via the job record's `status`/`progressPercent`; the finished artifact lands on `file`.

currentlyExporting.description: What the job is exporting right now.

file.description: File record IRI (or expanded record) of the exported archive.

template.description: Export template the job was created from.

ImportJob.description: An import job (`POST /api/3/import_jobs`): `options` carries the wizard's include/merge choices once populated; `logMessages` accumulates per-item import notes.

status.description: Job status; a `result` key carries progress notes (`Import job options populated`).

options.description: Wizard options: per-item `include` + `mergeType` for playbooks, modules, etc.

ImportJobStatus.description: Lightweight import-job status (`GET /api/import/{job_uuid}`): the job's `@type` plus a `status.result` note (e.g. `Import job options populated`). The full job record lives on `/api/3/import_jobs`.

LicenseInfo.description: License state (`GET /api/auth/license`). Multi-node fields (`*_nodes`) matter on HA setups; `POST /api/auth/license` (installing a license) is a privileged operation this spec documents but never exercises.

details.description: License details blob (serial, node id, product, version).

duplicate.description: True when another appliance runs the same license (FortiFlex conflict).

ClusterNodeHealth.description: One node's health row (`GET /api/auth/cluster/health` answers one per cluster node).

restricted_feature.description: Features the license tier does not unlock.

DailyActionCount.description: Workflow action budget (`GET /api/wf/workflow/config/`) -- the playbooks/day quota and what's left of it.

PermissionMap.description: The caller's effective permissions (`GET /api/permissions/current`): one entry per module/resource (e.g. `alerts`, `agents`, `ai_agents`) with its allowed operations.

alerts.description: Example entry; every module key follows the same shape.

CurrentUser.description: The authenticated principal (`GET /api/3/actors/current`): a Person-shaped record carrying the caller's `@permissions` block and `@settings` IRI.

@permissions.description: Effective permission flags for the caller.

AuditActivity.description: One audited activity row (`POST /api/gateway/audit/activities`): what changed, on which entity, by whom.

AuditActivityPage.description: Spring-style page of audit rows (`POST /api/gateway/audit/activities`) -- not hydra.

AuditCount.description: Row count for an audit filter (`POST /api/gateway/audit/activities/count`).

LlmActivityLog.description: One LLM call record (`/api/3/llm_activity_logs`): token counts, latency and cost per AI interaction.

correlationID.description: Ties the call to its trace/session.

error.description: Failure detail when status is failed.

DynamicVariable.description: A playbook dynamic variable (`/api/wf/api/dynamic-variable/`) -- global `$(variables)` available inside playbooks.

ViewConfig.description: A module view definition (`/api/views/1/{name}`): grid/list configuration for one module's UI.

ExportTemplate.description: An export template (`/api/3/export_templates`): the named, reusable selection of content an export job packages.

ExportTriggerResult.description: Result of `PUT /api/export` (query-param body): the created export job's reference.

last_publish_time.description: Epoch of the last successful publish.

WorkflowRun.description: One playbook run (`GET /api/wf/api/workflows/{pk}/`, rows of `historical-workflows` and the workflow-logs queries). `steps` carries the per-step rows (same shape as `GET /api/wf/api/historical-steps/`).

debug.description: True for debug runs (steps keep full I/O).

parent_wf.description: Parent run when this was spawned by another playbook.

template_iri.description: The playbook template that was executed.

HistoricalStep.description: One executed step (`GET /api/wf/api/historical-steps/`): the step's inputs, result and timing inside its parent run.

task_id.description: Run task id this step belongs to.

JinjaRenderResult.description: Rendered template (`POST /api/wf/api/jinja-editor/`) -- the Jinja editor's preview call.

task_id.description: Task id of the retried run.

AgentHeartbeat.description: One agent's heartbeat row (`GET /api/integration/agent-heartbeat/{agent}/`): connector + configuration the agent last reported, with its remote status.

action.description: Pending action for the agent, if any.

log_records.description: Log rows the agent has pending/processed.

tree.description: The connector's file tree after the write.

MCPServerRef.description: One entry of `GET /api/ai/mcp` -- the id + name the agent-config UI lists. Resolve to the full record on `/api/3/mcp_configurations`.

MCPHostedServer.description: Acknowledgment of `POST /mcp/add/tools` -- the hosted server's coordinates.

url.description: Gateway URL the server is served under.

MCPServerToolsExport.description: One server's exported tool catalog (`POST /mcp/config/export` answers a list of these).

restricted.description: Connectors that cannot be hosted (e.g. system connectors).

UserQuery.description: A saved query (`POST /api/3/user_queries`) -- the Search page's stored queries.

Router.description: A communication router (`GET /api/3/routers`) -- the mTLS endpoint agents and peers connect through.

MCPServerConfigInput.description: Create/update an MCP server registration. `authentication` is a JSON *string* (the appliance stores the block verbatim and never echoes secrets).

type.description: `FSR` for built-in gateways; `Custom` for external servers.

authentication.description: Auth block as a JSON string, e.g. `{"type": "FSR"}` or `{"type": "Bearer", "token": ...}`.

RoleCreate.description: Create a role. Only `name` is required; attach module grants afterwards via `PUT /api/3/roles/{uuid}` (pyfsr's `grant_module_permissions`).

TeamCreate.description: Create a team. `parents`/`children`/`siblings` place it in the ownership hierarchy (names, uuids or IRIs): parents see and edit child-owned records, children do not see each other, siblings share records both ways.

AgentAcceptanceRequest.description: Accept or reject an agent run's result (the human-in-the-loop gate).

accepted.description: `true` approves the run's result; `false` rejects it.

EnrichContextRequest.description: Store organizational context for enrichment (the `query` text is indexed for later IOC enrichment lookups).

MCPValidateRequest.description: Probe an MCP-server config *before* persisting it: FortiSOAR opens the connection and runs `tools/list`. `authentication` is a JSON **object** here (unlike the stored record, where it is a string).

uuid.description: Set when re-validating an already-registered server.

IngestionMetadataInput.description: Create a data-ingestion configuration: binds a connector configuration to ingestion playbooks and a schedule.

configuration.description: uuid of the connector configuration to bind.

connector.description: Connector reference (name + version; empty version = latest).

ViewConfigInput.description: Create/update a module view: grid/list layout for the module's UI.

MCPHostRequest.description: Host a connector's operations as MCP tools (`POST /mcp/add/tools`). Tool rows are keyed globally by name -- duplicates across servers silently drop. Requires the connector definition and a configuration first.

config.description: Connector configuration values for the hosted tools.

tools.description: One row per operation to host.

MCPToolsUpdateRequest.description: Update a hosted MCP server's tool set (`PUT /mcp/tools/{mcp_config_uuid}`): `tools` re-declares hosted rows, `remove_tools` unhosts by operation name.

MCPExportRequest.description: Servers to export (`POST /mcp/config/export`): one `{uuid}` object per registered server.

input_data.description: Payload the agent acts on; its shape is the agent's own `inputformat` schema (GET /api/ai/agent/{name}/{version}). For the shipped ioc-masking agent: `{"data": <text>, "action": "mask"}`.

context.description: Free-form execution context (the UI sends the page context).

user_id.description: Login id the run is attributed to.

task_id.description: Async task id: poll the status route, then fetch the result route.

status.description: `pending` while queued, `inprogress` while running, then `completed` or `failed`.

chain_of_thought.description: Reasoning steps, in order. Pass them back verbatim as `chain_of_thought` on POST /api/ai/insight/plan.

status.description: The plan was accepted for execution.

task_id.description: Async execution task id: poll GET /api/ai/insight/plan/{task_id}/status, then GET .../result.

referenceid.description: uuid of the saved insight record (the `insights` record POST /api/3/insights created).

createUser.description: IRI of the person the run is attributed to, e.g. `/api/3/people/{uuid}`.

valid.description: Whether the handshake + tools/list against the server succeeded.

tools.description: Tool names the server advertises (empty when `valid` is false).

message.description: Failure detail when `valid` is false (e.g. `MCP Configuration Failed! 401 Unauthorized`); null on success.

TriageAlertRequest.description: The alert to investigate: send the alert record's fields (as `GET /api/3/alerts/{uuid}` returns them) or at minimum a `name` reference (uuid, `alerts:<uuid>` or the record IRI).

Feasibility.title: Feasibility
Feasibility.description: Indicates whether the requested task can be completed with available agents and data.

type.description: How the input value should be interpreted by the agent.

value.title: Value
value.description: The actual input payload. Can be JSON configuration, or a reference to a previous step’s output.

knowledge.description: Semantic explanation of what this input represents and how it should be interpreted. Must refer specific fields, specific metrics

Input.title: Input
Input.description: A input required by an investigation step.

step_id.title: Step Id
step_id.description: Unique identifier for this step. Used for cross-step references.

title.title: Title
title.description: Short human-readable label summarizing what this step does.

description.title: Description
description.description: High-level explanation of what will be achieved after this step completes.

agent.title: Agent
agent.description: Name of the agent responsible for executing this step.

purpose.title: Purpose
purpose.description: Why this step exists and how it contributes to the overall mission objective. This should explain the step’s necessity, not how it is executed.

natural_language_task.title: Natural Language Task
natural_language_task.description: A full, unambiguous, self-contained instruction that the agent can execute directly. Must describe WHAT to do, not WHY.

inputs.title: Inputs
inputs.description: All inputs required by the agent to execute this step correctly. Each input must be explicitly justified via its Knowledge object.

role.title: Role
role.description: Role of this input in the step context. Typical values: 'instruction', 'configuration', 'produced_data'.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: Field-level semantic descriptions when the input contains structured data.

units.title: Units
units.description: Units associated with the data.Use a dict when different fields have different units.

calculation.title: Calculation
calculation.description: Human-readable description of how the data is calculated or derived, if applicable.

aggregation.title: Aggregation
aggregation.description: Aggregation logic applied to the data (e.g., avg, sum, count).

usage.title: Usage
usage.description: How this data is used in the step’s decision-making context (e.g., baseline measurement, SLA threshold, comparison input).

policy_mapping.title: Policy Mapping
policy_mapping.description: Explanation of how this operational data maps to policy, SLA, or organizational rules.

Knowledge.title: Knowledge
Knowledge.description:
Describes the semantic meaning of an input value.
Knowledge always explains WHAT the input represents and HOW it should be interpreted,
not what the agent should do procedurally.

objective.title: Objective
objective.description: The high-level goal provided by the user.

intent_interpretation.title: Intent Interpretation
intent_interpretation.description: High-level interpretation of the user's intent, without internal reasoning traces.

entities.title: Entities
entities.description: Specific module-level fields or attributes required for generating insights. These represent the exact data points (e.g., field names, parameters, or properties) that are referenced, analyzed, or correlated across investigation steps.

steps.title: Steps
steps.description: Ordered sequence of investigation steps. Each step must produce outputs consumed by subsequent steps.

Plan.title: Plan
Plan.description:
A structured investigation or analysis plan composed of ordered steps.
Each step must contribute directly to achieving the mission objective.
